doc.title: Bernie Kirsh interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 27, 2022

title: Chick's character and generosity
summary: Kirsh describes Chick as a beautiful, generous communicator; Rowe reads Kirsh's 2021 tribute.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Yeah. But you know Chick’s influence in my life was just huge. I mean he’s a guy who was a beautiful guy, just a beautiful guy. What you hear in his music is him. That’s his — the spirit of Chick is what you’re hearing and that’s how he was as a person. He was just beautiful, beautiful guy. And very kind of a generous guy. You know when you’re on the bandstand with somebody all of the social mechanisms that people employ in daily social interaction go away. You’re just there with another player playing the music and so you can get a feel for somebody that way. You know? Because you’re really dealing — it’s a spiritual activity, music. I mean you’re hearing it out of speakers and that’s the result of what had occurred before. But in the creative process, you know, you’re talking about someone’s decision to create beauty with somebody else. And the interplay of that is the heart of it. It’s why it happens. I mean there may be all kinds of other products that occur as a result of it, but that’s the essence of it, that relationship and in relationship eventually to the audience in a live situation where things are created in a live way. And Chick was a communicator of the highest level. Not only in his music but in life generally. That was one of his abilities. And so I think you find people who knew Chick would all agree that — I hear the same things over and over again, you know he lets people create. You know it’s basically allowing people to do what they do and grant them enough life to accept what they’re saying and not to put any negative aspect on it. That’s just what somebody else said, musically. And so you can like it or not like it but you don’t have to invalidate what the guy did. ‘Cause that’s invalidating him. And that’s something that it seemed to me that he didn’t — that I didn’t see him do. You know he would handle those things in another way than directly imposing something on someone’s artistry.

I see. This might be a good moment to read something, an excerpt from what you said about Chick. This is from May of 2021: “Yes he was a genius but that’s not enough of a descriptive word of all he was. He was generous as a musician as well as a person, and his love and support for other artists is unsurpassed. He loved to play with other musicians and when he did he did all he could to help musicians realize their most dear and personal artistic desires. It was just as important to see the others create with great satisfaction, as it was for him.”
Yeah. Well that’s basically it. Thanks for doing that, it saved me some words. I already said it.
